discovery: Discovery of high-energy astrophysical neutrinos and the opening of neutrino astronomy with IceCube
motivation: IceCube, a cubic-kilometre Cherenkov detector built in Antarctic ice, discovered in 2013 a diffuse flux of TeV-PeV neutrinos of extraterrestrial origin, now confirmed at high significance through independent channels. It has since identified the first sources: the blazar TXS 0506+056 (2017-18), the Seyfert galaxy NGC 1068 (2022) and neutrino emission from the Galactic plane (2023). These neutrinos are unambiguous tracers of hadronic acceleration, so they directly probe where cosmic rays are produced, a question open for a century. Halzen conceived the project and led it to completion; Karle led the detector design, construction and early analyses; Spiering pioneered deep-water and ice neutrino telescopes (Baikal, AMANDA) that proved the technique and shaped IceCube. Their work created a new observational window on the high-energy universe and lets theory be tested against multi-messenger data.
